text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to spin off its Ontario-based power generation assets into a limited partnership and offer units to the public.
TransCanada said it planned to keep a 50 percent interest in the new TransCanada Power LP and, after 20 years, fund the redemption of the partnership's outstanding units at then-fair market value.
The formation of the partnership followed a similar arrangement recently completed by Alberta Energy Co Ltd for its pipeline assets.

TransCanada said it filed a preliminary prospectus with Canadian securities commissions and expected the partnership units to be priced and issued in late May, with terms depending on market conditions at the time.
The offering was being led by Nesbitt Burns Inc and RBC Dominion Securities. Units would be made available to Canadian residents only.
TransCanada said it would use proceeds from the issue to fund part of its 1997 capital spending program.
The power assets included three enhanced combined-cycle plants at Nipigon, Kapuskasing and North Bay, Ontario.
Power produced by the plants is sold under long-term power purchase agreements with Ontario Hydro, TransCanada said.
